analysis:
Scope: a new offline model re-quantization tool (scripts/models/requant.py), a hash-pinned requirements file, and a test file. The test file's body was not supplied; only its metadata and patch excerpt were. The provider runtime, the coordinator and the attestation paths are untouched, so TB-002, TB-009 and TB-011 are unaffected directly. The relevant surface is the integrity of the model weights that providers later download (A-004, T-012, T-027). The output is intended to be uploaded to models.darkbloom.ai.

Examined:
- get() range reads check the exact length and retry with backoff. urllib.urlopen accepts any scheme and follows redirects, so URL validation is left to the caller (the workflow and upload-model-revision.py), which were not supplied.
- The source is expected to be a pinned 40-hex HF commit, but the tensor bytes are not hash-verified; the only integrity check is the later canonical manifest comparison, outside the supplied evidence.
- Template files are copied without checking the manifest sha256 (see the path-containment finding at lines 401-410).
- Header parsing reads untrusted JSON offsets and sizes. The risk is limited to memory and DoS on the build machine.
- The quantizer arithmetic and selftest golden digests look deterministic. The selftest is a reproducibility gate, not an authenticity control, and its digests live in the same file as the code.
- requirements-requant-upload.txt uses hashes for the named packages (--require-hashes) and wheel-only installs, which is good supply-chain hygiene. I could not verify the hash values against PyPI.

Open questions for deeper review: the .github/workflows/model-requant-upload.yml permissions and secret handling (R2 credentials), input validation of the template and source URLs, how upload-model-revision.py gates publication to production, and the contents of test_model_requant_upload.py.

findings.detail: cmd_build reads manifest.json from the remote template URL and, for every non-model entry, writes the downloaded bytes to os.path.join(a.out, f["path"]). The path is never checked for absolute components, ".." segments or path separators. A compromised or mistaken template manifest, or a template URL pointed at an attacker-controlled host, could make the build write files outside the output directory on the CI runner or a developer Mac. Within the output directory it could also overwrite the regenerated config.json or index, since only the names "config.json" and "model.safetensors.index.json" are skipped. The copied files are not verified against the manifest sha256 either. Fix: reject any path that is not a plain relative basename or normalized subpath, resolve it under a.out and assert containment, and verify each copied file's size and hash against the manifest before writing.
findings.title: requant.py build writes template-manifest paths to disk without containment checks
